LifeKindled

LifeKindled is a Bible reading and community companion built for families, churches, and small groups. It brings scripture, prayer, worship, and discussion into one shared space, so growing in faith feels like something you do together, not alone.

It isn't just a Bible app.It's a shared space for showing up for your faith, together.

View on the App Store
What Is LifeKindled?

Faith, kept in one place.

Faith often gets scattered—a reading plan here, a prayer list there, a group chat that goes quiet after a few weeks.

LifeKindled brings it together. Scripture in NLT, NKJV, CSB, or KJV, guided and free-form prayer, a worship timer, and discussions tied to your group's daily reading all live in one place—so consistency feels natural instead of forced.

Every feature is built with one purpose: helping your family, church, or group show up for each other, one day at a time.

Built Around Your Community

Made for groups of every size.

Whether it's a family devotional, a youth group, or a full congregation, LifeKindled adapts to how your community already gathers. Leaders can set reading plans with built-in rest days, invite members with a simple code, and see who's engaging through a dedicated dashboard.

Everyone else just opens the app and reads, prays, and reflects—together.

Thoughtfully Designed

Consistency over guilt.

LifeKindled tracks your reading, prayer, and worship streaks to celebrate showing up—not to shame you for missing a day. Every screen is built to keep your attention on scripture, not on the app itself.

No clutter. No pressure. Just scripture, prayer, and your people.

Why LifeKindled?

There are countless Bible apps. There are countless group chats. LifeKindled brings the best of both together.

Not another app competing for your attention—
but one built to point it toward scripture.
Not a solitary reading plan—
but a reason to show up for your people.
Not a substitute for your church—
but a way to stay connected between Sundays.
The Future Belongs to Creators.

Kindle something worth passing on.

Whether it's your family around the table or a congregation reading together, every meaningful habit starts with a single day.
